slides.say: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle whose legs are eight centimeters and fifteen centimeters. What is the radius of the circle, in centimeters?

Inscribed in the triangle means the circle sits inside it and touches all three sides. So every side of the triangle is a tangent to the circle. [short pause] We'll use the tangent rules, and at the end there's a short formula too.

[short pause] First the third side, the hypotenuse. Eight squared is sixty-four, fifteen squared is two hundred twenty-five, and together that's two hundred eighty-nine. Eight, fifteen, seventeen is a Pythagorean triple, and seventeen squared really is two hundred eighty-nine. So the hypotenuse is seventeen.

Now the tangent rule. The sides are tangents, so I draw the radii to the two legs. Each radius is perpendicular to its leg. With the right angle of the triangle, we get a little square, r by r, in the corner.
So the corner pieces of the legs are r and r. The rest of the short leg is eight minus r, and the rest of the long leg is fifteen minus r.

Now the second rule. Two tangents from the same point are equal. From the top corner come two tangents, so the top piece of the hypotenuse is also eight minus r. From the bottom corner on the right, the other piece is fifteen minus r.
These two pieces make the whole hypotenuse, seventeen. So eight minus r plus fifteen minus r is seventeen.
Eight plus fifteen is twenty-three, so twenty-three minus two r is seventeen. Then two r is twenty-three minus seventeen, which is six, and r is three. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] The same equation in one line gives a shortcut for a right triangle. The radius of the circle inside is leg plus leg minus the hypotenuse, over two.
at: The same equation in one line

slides.say: Eight plus fifteen minus seventeen is six, and half of six is three. Careful, six is in the choices too. That's someone who forgot to divide by two.
at: someone who forgot to divide by two

slides.say: And eight and a half is half of the hypotenuse. Remember, in a right triangle the hypotenuse is a diameter of the circle around the triangle. So eight and a half is the radius of the circle around it, not inside it. The answer is three, choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
